title: BKT universality for height and planar spin fields
main_claim: For every finite square-symmetric interaction J containing nearest neighbours, the 2D discrete Gaussian height model has a Gaussian free field torus limit for all beta >= beta_c(J), and the threshold itself is rough. The effective temperature takes the universal endpoint value 8*pi*v_J^2 (2*pi for nearest neighbours), with infinite right slope, differentiability above beta_c, and beta_eff = beta + O(e^{-c beta}). For the Villain and XY models at sufficiently low fixed temperature, the Green-normalised spin fields converge to imaginary chaos V_{K,D}, with K_Villain(b) = beta_eff(J_nn, pi^2 b)/pi^2.

issues.location: sections/entry.tex, Theorem en:entry (Local entry at every positive coefficient) and its use in sections/endpoint.tex
issues.description: Not a demonstrated gap, but the main load-bearing input I could not check line by line. Every endpoint conclusion (a(k_c)=8pi through openness, the critical state strip, the infinite slope) depends on the entry theorem. That theorem supplies small analytic activities on a neighbourhood U of (k_h,a_h), with k-derivative bounds, which includes inputs on both sides of k_h. The openness argument needs entry at inputs k < k_h where a(k) may be 0. The statement does allow this, since U is a neighbourhood in k and no scaling hypothesis is imposed off k_h. Its proof (about 1250 lines plus the mixed-pin results in annular.tex) was only skimmed.
issues.evidence: 'No uniform scaling assertion at temperatures other than k_h is part of either the hypotheses or the proof.' Used in ep:supermarginal: 'Choose k_-<k_h<k_+ ... u_infty(k_-,a_h)<0'

issues.description: The endpoint argument uses only the signs and positivity of H and b. I checked b = 2 log L independently from lambda = L^{2-a'/(4pi)} with a_eff = a'(1+u). I did not re-derive the explicit constant H_en = (8pi*pi/4) e^{8pi c} log L. Its positivity is consistent with screening lowering the effective coefficient, so the argument does not depend on the exact value.

coverage: Read in full: the introduction and the statements of all main theorems. Read in full and checked: structural.tex, which covers the lattice Gaussian comparisons via Cauchy-Schwarz and Poisson; free-rectangle saturation through cutting and folding; the fractional-mean replica argument, where I re-derived the identity -2(FF''-F'^2), Cov(X,Y) -> a/2 and the Q=l sector mean; the face-ratio lemma, where the exponent G^{2-a/(4pi)} follows from sum D^2 = (1/2pi) log G and the Hessian lower bound; the charge-gap corollary; and zero-coefficient localization, including the penalty identity sum Q^2 = sum n^2 - l^2/G^2 and the local-limit ratio. Also checked: in annular.tex, the physical criterion (log-pole energy 2pi log(1/delta)) and coefficient regularity (U' >= U^2/k^2, giving 1/a(k2) <= 1/a(k1) + 1/k2 - 1/k1); and all of endpoint.tex. For endpoint.tex I re-derived: phase factorization; the no-exit argument; Gaussian curves; the response inequality; the openness/IVT argument giving a(k_c)=8pi; odd-sector non-exponential decay from the face ratio; the state strip and the barrier computation, including x_{j+1}-x_j = (bx^2-H)Z, Z_j ~ 1/j and x -> sqrt(H/b); the derivative matrix M, with eigenvalues d0 and -2d0 and unstable eigenvector (1, -sqrt(b/H)/2), which I recomputed; and the warm crossover with p_infty -> infinity and the mean-value step. In weak-height.tex I read the gapped shooting, the high-temperature corollary and the spread-out corollary (k_0 = 8pi). For the spin results I checked the normalisation constants only: Villain duality beta = pi^2 b, K = beta_eff/pi^2, the endpoint 2/pi, and the imaginary-chaos threshold K > 1/(4pi). Not line-checked: the entry.tex analytic construction; the annular exploration and pin propositions; the toolkit; the Villain and XY history/flow sections (villain.tex, xy-histories.tex, xy-flow.tex); and the weak-height map estimates.
sibling_notes: The family-216 board had two entries: the Critical Center Magnetization paper (rank 104) and the critical logarithmic correction paper (rank 95). Both were no_gap_found, and both rely on companions for a(b_c)=8pi and the local maps. This paper appears to be one of those companions: it proves a(k_c)=8pi and builds the local and entry maps. The siblings' checks of the separatrix and invariant structure match the state-strip analysis here, where x -> sqrt(H/b) and Z ~ 1/j. That agreement supports the consistency of the family but does not replace an audit of entry.tex.
